explanation: $Q = It = 3011.86~\text{C}$. $n_e = \frac{Q}{F} = 0.0312~\text{mol}$. The ion requires $2~\text{mol}$ of electrons per mole of metal, so $n_{\text{metal}} = \frac{0.0312}{2} = 0.0156~\text{mol}$. Mass = $n \times M = (0.0156)(65.4) \approx 1.02~\text{g}$.

question: Calculate the energy difference (in eV) between the $n=4$ and $n=1$ energy levels of a hydrogen atom. ($1~\text{eV} = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}~\text{J}$)
explanation: Energy levels in hydrogen: $E_n = \frac{-13.6}{n^2}~\text{eV}$. $\Delta E = E_{4} - E_{1} = \frac{-13.6}{4^2} - \frac{-13.6}{1^2} = 12.78~\text{eV}$ (magnitude).
